Help.Title: Help & Instructions
Help.Intro: Quick guide for safely managing native Hyper-V VM groups without SCVMM.
Help.OverviewText: Hyper-V VM Group Manager manages native VMCollectionType groups on standalone Hyper-V hosts or failover clusters. These groups can be used as stable backup objects in Veeam. A VM may belong to multiple groups.
Help.WorkflowText: All actions are initially planned locally. The VM and group lists already show the expected target state. Only “Validate and apply” sends the complete change set to the target server.
Help.QuickStartText:
1. Enter a host or cluster name and select “Connect”.

2. Select an existing backup group or create one with “+ New”.

3. Select one or more VMs and add or remove them.

4. Review the change preview.

5. Select “Validate and apply” and confirm the safety prompt.
Help.FiltersText: VM search includes name, state, owner node, and group names. The filter can show VMs without a group or only members of the selected group, among other options.
Help.SafetyText: Before writing, the target, server snapshot, and change set are validated. Invalid names, duplicate objects, contradictory memberships, and deletion of non-empty groups are blocked. After an uncertain or cancelled write operation, a refresh is mandatory.
Help.RefreshText: “Refresh” reloads the server state and retains valid planned changes. “Discard” removes all local planned changes. Prompts prevent accidental loss when switching targets or closing the app.
Help.ReportingText: Under “Settings”, configure the SMTP server, sender, recipients, and a daily scheduled task. The report lists VMs without a group assignment. Credentials are protected per user with Windows DPAPI.
Help.ReportingWarning: Important: A scheduled task must run as the same Windows user who stored the SMTP credentials. Test the configuration with “Send now” first.
Help.RequirementsText: Windows PowerShell 5.1, the Hyper-V module, and sufficient permissions on the target are required. Failover Clustering cmdlets must be available for clusters. Remote access needs appropriate WinRM and firewall configuration.
Help.LogsText: Application logs are stored under %LocalAppData%\HyperVGroupManager. For connection errors, check DNS resolution, permissions, PowerShell modules, and remote management first. After a timeout or cancellation, always run “Refresh” first.
Help.LanguageText: The language can be switched between German and English at any time in the upper-right corner. The selection is stored only in the local user profile; the portable application folder remains unchanged.
Settings.ScheduleDescription: The report is sent daily at the specified time and lists all VMs that are not assigned to a Hyper-V group. The task runs under the current Windows user account.
